category: Text, Tables, Leaders, Dimension Editing & Annotation Scaling
description: The second tier of annotation tools: text conversion, scaling, justification and alignment commands, spelling and find/replace, fields, the text Express Tools (numbering, case, arc text, masks, remote text), table editing and export, multileader styles and alignment, quick leaders and geometric tolerance frames, associative centre marks and centrelines, the dimension editing commands that complement DIMEDIT/DIMSTYLE (text placement, inspection, reassociation, jog lines, overrides), multiline editing, and the annotative-scaling commands and variables that decide which scale representations exist and are visible.

tools.name: TXT2MTXT
tools.description: Converts one or more single-line TEXT objects into a multiline MTEXT object, or combines several MTEXT objects into one, keeping the position of the first line and optionally re-flowing the text with word wrap. Originally an Express Tool, it has been a core command since 2017.1 and is the standard clean-up for text imported from PDFs, DXF translations or old drawings drawn line by line.
tools.usage:
TXT2MTXT
Select text objects or [SEttings]: <selection> Enter
Settings dialog: Combine into a single mtext object, Sort top-down, Create word-wrap MText, Force uniform line spacing

parameters.name: Combine into a single mtext object
parameters.description: One MTEXT from all selected lines; unchecked converts each TEXT to its own MTEXT.

parameters.name: Sort top-down
parameters.description: Order lines by Y position rather than selection order.

parameters.name: Create word-wrap MText
parameters.description: Ignore the original line breaks and let the MTEXT width wrap the paragraph.

parameters.name: Force uniform line spacing
parameters.description: Regular spacing instead of reproducing the original gaps.

tools.example:
TXT2MTXT
SE
(tick Combine, Sort top-down, untick Word-wrap, OK)
(select the 8 lines of the general notes) Enter
tools.notes: The text style and height of the first object are used for the result; mixed styles are lost. Attributes and dimension text are not eligible. Available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: SCALETEXT
tools.description: Changes the height of many text, MTEXT and attribute objects at once, scaling each about its own justification point (or a chosen one) so nothing moves, unlike SCALE which uses one base point. The new size can be a model height, a paper height for annotative-style workflows, a factor, or matched from another object.
tools.usage:
SCALETEXT
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Enter a base point option for scaling [Existing/Left/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <Existing>:
Specify new model height or [Paper height/Match object/Scale factor] <2.5>:

parameters.name: base point option
parameters.description: Existing keeps each object's own justification; the others scale about that corner/side of each object.

parameters.name: Paper height
parameters.description: Height on paper; converted using the current annotation scale (CANNOSCALE) for non-annotative text.

parameters.name: Match object
parameters.description: Copy the height of a picked text object.

parameters.name: Scale factor
parameters.description: Multiply the current heights (or use Reference).

tools.example:
SCALETEXT
(select all room labels) Enter
E
P
2.5
tools.notes: Works on TEXT, MTEXT and ATTRIB objects but not on dimension text (use DIMSTYLE/DIMTXT) or table cells. For annotative text prefer adding scales with OBJECTSCALE rather than changing height.

tools.name: JUSTIFYTEXT
tools.description: Changes the justification (insertion) point of selected text, MTEXT, leader text and attribute objects without moving the text on screen - the text stays where it is and the grip/insertion point relocates. Useful before stretching or aligning text, or to standardise labels to Middle Center so they rotate about their centre.
tools.usage:
JUSTIFYTEXT
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Enter a justification option [Left/Align/Fit/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <Left>:

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: Standard TEXT justifications; MTEXT accepts the nine TL..BR options.

tools.example:
JUSTIFYTEXT
(select the door tags) Enter
MC
tools.notes: The Express Tool TJUST does the same. Changing justification of MTEXT also changes its flow direction when the width is later edited.

tools.name: TEXTALIGN
tools.description: Aligns several text, MTEXT or attribute objects to a reference text object or to two picked points, vertically, horizontally or along an oblique line, with optional even distribution or fixed spacing (2015+). It replaces the tedious move-by-osnap routine for lining up notes, schedule rows and tag columns.
tools.usage:
TEXTALIGN  (alias TA)
Select text objects to align [alIgnment/Options]: <selection> Enter
Select text object to align to or [Points]: <pick reference text> | P then two points
(drag to set direction; Options: Distribute, Set spacing, Currently vertical/horizontal)

parameters.name: alIgnment
parameters.description: Which justification point of each object is aligned: Left/Center/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR.

parameters.name: Options > Distribute / Set spacing
parameters.description: Spread the objects evenly between the first and last, or place them a fixed distance apart (TEXTALIGNSPACING).

parameters.name: Points
parameters.description: Align along a line defined by two points instead of to another text object.

parameters.name: TEXTALIGNMODE
parameters.description: Remembers the last alignment option.

tools.example:
TEXTALIGN
(select the five note lines) Enter
O
S
5
(pick the top note as the reference, drag downward, click)
tools.notes: Objects keep their own justification unless alIgnment overrides it. Works on TEXT, MTEXT and attributes only; MLEADER text is aligned with MLEADERALIGN.

tools.name: SPACETRANS
tools.description: Transparent command that converts a length between model space and paper space using the scale of the current viewport, so a text height or offset can be typed in paper units while working in a viewport (or in model units while in a layout). Prefix it with an apostrophe inside another command's numeric prompt; the converted value is fed back to that prompt.
tools.usage:
'SPACETRANS  (inside a command, at a distance/height prompt)
In a layout viewport (model space active): Specify paper space distance <1.0>: <value>  -> returns the model-space equivalent
In paper space: Specify model space distance <1.0>: <value>  -> returns the paper-space equivalent (also asks for a viewport if several exist)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The length in the other space; the result is value multiplied or divided by the viewport scale.

tools.example:
; inside a 1:50 viewport, create text that plots 2.5 mm high
TEXT
(pick point)
'SPACETRANS
2.5
(returns 125 as the height)
0
ROOM 101
tools.notes: Only meaningful in a layout; in the Model tab it returns the input unchanged. Annotative text (with CANNOSCALE set) makes this unnecessary, but SPACETRANS is still useful for offsets and hatch scales.

tools.name: TEXTTOFRONT
tools.description: Brings all text, dimensions and/or leaders in the drawing to the top of the draw order in one step so they are never hidden by hatches, wipeouts or solid fills, and HATCHTOBACK sends every hatch to the bottom. Together they are the standard fix for annotation buried under fills, and both are what the DRAWORDERCTL-aware draw order tools run for the whole drawing.
tools.usage:
TEXTTOFRONT
Bring to front [Text/Dimensions/Leaders/All] <All>:
HATCHTOBACK  (no prompts; all hatches sent to back)

parameters.name: Text / Dimensions / Leaders / All
parameters.description: Which annotation classes to bring forward; Leaders covers LEADER and MLEADER objects.

parameters.name: HPDRAWORDER
parameters.description: Default draw order for new hatches: 0 none, 1 send to back (default), 2 bring to front, 3 behind boundary, 4 in front of boundary.

tools.example:
; Script clean-up before plotting
HATCHTOBACK
TEXTTOFRONT
A
REGEN
tools.notes: Draw order is stored per space in the SortEnts table; xref content is ordered inside the xref. Changing draw order marks the drawing modified. Works in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: SPELL
tools.description: Runs the Check Spelling dialog over the whole drawing, the current space/layout or a selection, checking text, MTEXT, dimension text, multileaders, attributes, table cells and optionally xrefs against the main dictionary (DCTMAIN) and a custom word list (DCTCUST). It offers Ignore/Ignore All/Add to Dictionary/Change/Change All and zooms to each hit. In-editor spell checking (red underline in MTEXT) is separate and controlled in the MTEXT ribbon.
tools.usage:
SPELL
(Check Spelling dialog: Where to check [Entire drawing / Current space/layout / Selected objects], Start, Settings, Dictionaries)

parameters.name: Where to check
parameters.description: Entire drawing, current space or a selection made with the pick button.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Include dimension text, block attributes, external references; ignore capitalised words, words with numbers, uppercase words, mixed case, punctuation.

parameters.name: DCTMAIN / DCTCUST
parameters.description: System variables naming the language dictionary (e.g. enu, ena, deu) and the custom .cus file.

tools.example:
DCTMAIN enu
SPELL
(Entire drawing, Start, review each flagged word)
tools.notes: Cannot be scripted meaningfully because it is dialog-driven; there is no command-line variant. Words added with Add go to DCTCUST, which can be shared across a team on the network.

tools.name: FIND
tools.description: Find and Replace for text across the drawing: searches single-line and multiline text, dimension and leader text, block attribute values, table cells and hyperlinks (optionally inside xrefs) with match-case, whole-word and wildcard options, listing every hit with a zoom-to button and offering Replace or Replace All. It is the tool for renaming a project number or fixing a misspelt term everywhere in one go.
tools.usage:
FIND
(Find and Replace dialog: Find what, Replace with, Find where [Entire drawing / Current space/layout / Selected objects], expand for Search options and Text types, List results, Replace / Replace All / Find)

parameters.name: Search options
parameters.description: Match case, Find whole words only, Use wildcards, Search xrefs, Search blocks, Ignore hidden items, Match diacritics, Match half/full width forms.

parameters.name: Text types
parameters.description: Block attribute value, Dimension or leader text, Single-line/multiline text, Table text, Hyperlink description, Hyperlink.

parameters.name: List results
parameters.description: Table of matches with location and object type; select rows to zoom, or Create selection set.

tools.example:
FIND
(Find what: P-1041, Replace with: P-1042, Find where: Entire drawing, tick Block attribute value, Replace All)
-> 'Replaced 14 occurrences'
tools.notes: Replacements inside MTEXT preserve formatting codes only when the match does not straddle a code. FIND does not search field code text (the evaluated value only) nor text inside blocks unless Search blocks is ticked. For scripts use AutoLISP with vl-string-subst on entget data or the FIND-like (vla-put-TextString) loops.

tools.name: UPDATEFIELD
tools.description: Forces the fields in selected objects (or all objects) to re-evaluate immediately - sheet numbers, plot dates, object properties, formulas in tables, Diesel expressions - instead of waiting for the events listed in FIELDEVAL. Used in scripts right before plotting or publishing so title-block fields such as date and file name are current.
tools.usage:
UPDATEFIELD
Select objects: <selection or ALL> Enter
FIELDEVAL = bit sum: 1 update on open, 2 on save, 4 on plot, 8 on eTransmit, 16 on regen (default 31 = all)
FIELDDISPLAY = 0 no grey background behind fields, 1 grey background (default; never plots)

parameters.name: Select objects
parameters.description: Text, MTEXT, attributes, tables and multileaders containing fields; type ALL for everything.

parameters.name: FIELDEVAL 0
parameters.description: Fields are never updated automatically - useful when a drawing must show the date it was issued rather than the current date.

tools.example:
; Script prelude
UPDATEFIELD
ALL

-PLOT ...

; AutoLISP
(command "_.UPDATEFIELD" "_ALL" "")
tools.notes: Fields inside block definitions are updated per reference. A field showing #### means the object it references was erased or the expression is invalid - edit it with the in-place editor (double-click) and Edit Field. The Core Console honours FIELDEVAL on save and plot.

tools.name: TEXTMASK
tools.description: Express Tool that places a background mask behind selected text or MTEXT objects so linework underneath is hidden, using a WIPEOUT, a 3D FACE or a 2D SOLID sized by an offset factor times the text height. The mask is grouped with the text and moves with it. TEXTUNMASK removes it. MTEXT has a native Background Mask property that is preferable for MTEXT; TEXTMASK is the option for single-line TEXT.
tools.usage:
TEXTMASK
Current settings: Offset factor = 0.35, Mask type = Wipeout
Select text objects to mask or [Masktype/Offset]: <selection> | M | O
Masktype: [Wipeout/3dface/Solid]
TEXTUNMASK  Select text or MText object from which mask is to be removed:

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Margin around the text as a multiple of the text height (default 0.35).

parameters.name: Masktype
parameters.description: Wipeout (default; hides everything, plots blank), 3dface (hidden-line style, respects draw order), Solid (a filled 2D solid in a chosen colour).

tools.example:
TEXTMASK
O
0.5
(select the pipe labels) Enter
tools.notes: Wipeout masks can print as black rectangles on some plotters/PDF drivers when raster output is limited - test the plot. Masked text moved with grips drags its mask because the two are grouped (PICKSTYLE must include group selection). Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: TCOUNT
tools.description: Express Tool that numbers selected text and MTEXT objects sequentially, sorting them by X, Y or selection order and writing the number as a prefix, suffix, replacement or into a placeholder found with find-and-replace. It is the fastest way to number notes, keynotes or parking bays after they have been placed.
tools.usage:
TCOUNT
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Sort selected objects by [X/Y/Select-order] <Y>:
Specify starting number and increment (Start,increment) <1,1>:
Placement of numbers in text [Overwrite/Prefix/Suffix/Find&replace..] <Prefix>:

parameters.name: Sort
parameters.description: X left-to-right, Y top-to-bottom, or the order in which the objects were picked.

parameters.name: Placement
parameters.description: Overwrite replaces the whole string; Prefix/Suffix add the number (with a space); Find&replace substitutes a token such as ## with the number.

tools.example:
TCOUNT
(select the keynote texts) Enter
Y
1,1
P
tools.notes: Attributes and dimension text are not numbered. Numbers are plain text, not fields. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: TCASE
tools.description: Express Tool that changes the case of selected text, MTEXT, attributes and dimension text to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case or toggled case via a small dialog. The MTEXT in-place editor has its own case buttons; TCASE is for doing many objects at once.
tools.usage:
TCASE
Select objects: <selection> Enter
(TCASE - Change Text Case dialog: Sentence case / lowercase / UPPERCASE / Title / tOGGLE cASE)
tools.example:
TCASE
(select all annotation on the sheet) Enter
(UPPERCASE, OK)
tools.notes: TEXTALLCAPS (2015+) forces new text to uppercase as it is typed, which avoids the need for TCASE on new drawings. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: ARCTEXT
tools.description: Places text along an arc, with the ArcAlignedText Workshop dialog controlling text, style, font, height, width factor, offsets from the arc, alignment (fit, left, right, centre, and reading direction inward/outward), and reverse direction. The result is a custom ArcAlignedText object that stays editable with the same command. An Express Tool for decades, it became a core command (and is in LT) with AutoCAD 2023.
tools.usage:
ARCTEXT
Select an Arc or an ArcAlignedText: <pick arc>
(ArcAlignedText Workshop dialog: Text field, Style, Font, Height, Width factor, Char spacing, Offset from arc, Left/Right offsets, Alignment: Fit/Left/Right/Center, Position: Inward/Outward to center, Reverse, Underline, Bold/Italic, Color)

parameters.name: Alignment
parameters.description: Fit stretches the text along the whole arc; Left/Right/Center place it from an end or the middle.

parameters.name: Offset from arc
parameters.description: Distance from the arc to the text baseline; negative or Convex/Concave settings put text inside or outside.

parameters.name: Reverse
parameters.description: Flip the reading direction along the arc.

tools.example:
ARC (draw a 90-degree arc)
ARCTEXT
(pick the arc; type NORTH ELEVATION, height 3.5, Center, OK)
tools.notes: ArcAlignedText is a custom object from the Express Tools DBX module; drawings opened where it is missing (older releases, some third-party viewers) show a proxy or nothing. EXPLODE turns it into individual TEXT objects. TXTEXP can convert it to polylines.

tools.name: TORIENT
tools.description: Express Tool that rotates text, MTEXT, attribute definitions and blocks with attributes about their own insertion points so they read correctly: Most Readable flips anything upside-down or reading right-to-left, or a fixed absolute angle can be applied to everything. Standard tool after rotating or mirroring a plan.
tools.usage:
TORIENT
Select objects: <selection> Enter
New absolute rotation <Most Readable>: Enter | <angle>

parameters.name: Most Readable
parameters.description: Each object is rotated 180 degrees only if it currently reads from right to left or upside-down.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Absolute rotation applied to every selected object.

tools.example:
MIRROR (plan, MIRRTEXT 0)
TORIENT
(select the labels) Enter

(Most Readable)
tools.notes: MIRRTEXT 0 already prevents mirrored text; TORIENT fixes the cases where text was rotated by ROTATE. Objects are rotated about their justification point, so alignment along a line is preserved. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: TSCALE
tools.description: Express Tool that scales text, MTEXT, attributes and attribute definitions about a chosen point of each object to a new height, a matched height or a factor - the same job as the core SCALETEXT (which grew out of it) but with attribute definitions included, which SCALETEXT ignores.
tools.usage:
TSCALE
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Enter a base point option for scaling [Existing/Left/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <Existing>:
Specify new height or [Match/Scale factor] <2.5>:

parameters.name: Match
parameters.description: Copy the height from a picked text object.

parameters.name: Scale factor
parameters.description: Multiply current heights.

tools.example:
TSCALE
(select the ATTDEFs in the exploded title block) Enter
E
3
tools.notes: Use SCALETEXT in scripts that must also run in AutoCAD LT. Not in LT.

tools.name: TEXTFIT
tools.description: Express Tool that stretches or compresses a single-line TEXT object to fit between two points by changing its width factor, without changing its height. It is how labels are made to fit inside a fixed-width cell or between two grid lines on legacy drawings.
tools.usage:
TEXTFIT
Select Text to stretch/shrink: <pick>
Specify end point or [Start point]: <point> | S then two points

parameters.name: end point
parameters.description: The text is scaled from its current start to this point.

parameters.name: Start point
parameters.description: Redefine both ends.

tools.example:
TEXTFIT
(pick the label)
(click the right edge of the box)
tools.notes: Only TEXT, not MTEXT. The width factor is stored as the object's Width property and can be reset to 1 in Properties. Not in LT.

tools.name: RTEXT
tools.description: Express Tool that creates Remote Text: a text object whose content is the contents of an external text file (re-read when the drawing opens or REGEN runs) or the evaluated result of a DIESEL expression. Classic uses are a shared notes file that many drawings display, and DIESEL stamps such as the drawing path and plot date before fields existed. RTEDIT edits an existing rtext object.
tools.usage:
RTEXT
Current settings: Style=Standard Height=2.5 Rotation=0
Enter an option [Style/Height/Rotation/File/Diesel] <File>:
File: (select .txt file)   Diesel: (Edit RText dialog: expression)
Specify start point of RText:
RTEDIT  Select an RText: ... [Style/Height/Rotation/Edit]

parameters.name: File
parameters.description: External ASCII file; the rtext shows its lines and updates when the file changes.

parameters.name: Diesel
parameters.description: A DIESEL string such as $(getvar,dwgprefix)$(getvar,dwgname) or Plotted $(edtime,$(getvar,date),DD/MO/YYYY).

parameters.name: Style / Height / Rotation
parameters.description: Text style, height and angle of the rtext object.

tools.example:
RTEXT
H
2.5
D
$(getvar,dwgprefix)$(getvar,dwgname) - $(edtime,$(getvar,date),DD MON YYYY HH:MM)
(click the start point)
tools.notes: Rtext is a custom object; use FIELD for new work because fields are native and plot everywhere. The path in File mode is absolute unless REDIR is used to remap it. Not in LT.

tools.name: TABLEDIT
tools.description: Edits the text of a single table cell in place with the MTEXT editor - the same as double-clicking a cell. Cell content can be plain text, a field or a formula (=SUM(A2:A9), =A1*B1, =AVERAGE, =COUNT); pressing Tab moves to the next cell so a column can be typed quickly. For structural edits (rows, columns, merge, cell styles) select the cell and use the Table Cell contextual ribbon or the Properties palette.
tools.usage:
TABLEDIT
Pick a table cell: <click inside the cell>
(type text; Tab / Shift+Tab move between cells; Esc or click outside to finish)
Formulas: =SUM(B2:B12)  =A2*1.2  =COUNT(C2:C30)  =AVERAGE(D2:D5)  ; cell references use column letters and row numbers as in a spreadsheet

parameters.name: Cell reference
parameters.description: A1-style; ranges as A1:B5; cells in another table by table name via the Field dialog.

parameters.name: Fields in cells
parameters.description: Right-click > Insert Field; e.g. a block attribute or an object's area.

parameters.name: Cell lock
parameters.description: Data-linked tables lock content by default - unlock through the ribbon before editing.

tools.example:
TABLEDIT
(click cell B2) 12.50 Tab 8.75 Tab 3.10 Esc
TABLEDIT
(click B5) =SUM(B2:B4) Esc
tools.notes: Formulas recalculate when UPDATEFIELD runs or FIELDEVAL events fire. Text height and style come from the cell style in the TABLESTYLE unless overridden. TABLEDIT is what CUI double-click actions map for AcDbTable.

tools.name: TABLESTYLE
tools.description: Creates and modifies table styles - named sets of cell styles (Title, Header, Data plus custom ones) each with General (fill colour, alignment, format, type, margins), Text (style, height, colour, angle) and Borders (lineweight, linetype, colour, double line) settings, and a table direction (Down or Up). The current style (CTABLESTYLE) is used by TABLE and by DATAEXTRACTION output; keeping schedules consistent across a project means keeping table styles in the template.
tools.usage:
TABLESTYLE
(Table Style dialog: Styles list, Set Current, New, Modify, Delete; per cell style: General / Text / Borders tabs; Table direction)
CTABLESTYLE = name of the current table style (system variable)

parameters.name: Starting table
parameters.description: Pick an existing table in the drawing to seed a new style with its formatting.

parameters.name: Cell styles
parameters.description: Title, Header, Data are built in; Create new cell style adds e.g. Subtotal. Each has fill, alignment, data format (Angle/Currency/Date/Decimal/General/Percentage/Point/Text/Whole number), margins.

parameters.name: Table direction
parameters.description: Down (title at top) or Up (title at bottom, rows added upward, used for bill-of-materials on title blocks).

parameters.name: Borders
parameters.description: Apply lineweight/colour/linetype to all, outside, inside, or individual edges; double line with spacing.

tools.example:
TABLESTYLE
(New: 'SCHEDULE', start from Standard; Data cell: text height 2.5, alignment Middle Left; Header: fill colour 254; OK, Set Current)
TABLE (creates a 5x4 table in the SCHEDULE style)
tools.notes: Cell-level overrides made on a table (colours, heights) survive style changes; remove them with the ribbon's Remove All Property Overrides. Styles are purgeable when unused and can be imported through DesignCenter.

tools.name: TABLEEXPORT
tools.description: Exports the contents of a table object to a CSV (comma-separated) file that Excel and databases open directly. Only the cell text/values are written - no formatting, merged-cell structure or formulas - one row per table row. Handy for quantity schedules built with DATAEXTRACTION that must be sent onward, and it works in scripts since the file path is the only input.
tools.usage:
TABLEEXPORT
Select a table: <pick>
(Export Data dialog: file name .csv)

parameters.name: file name
parameters.description: CSV path; a FILEDIA 0 session prompts at the command line instead.

tools.example:
TABLEEXPORT
(pick the door schedule)
C:/proj/door_schedule.csv
tools.notes: Fields are exported as their current values. For the reverse direction use DATALINK (Excel to table) or PASTESPEC. The ActiveX AcadTable object exposes GetText/GetCellValue for custom exports.

tools.name: TINSERT
tools.description: Inserts a block into a table cell, scaled to fit the cell or at an explicit scale, with rotation and alignment options - the way symbol legends and 'image' columns in schedules are built. The block becomes the cell's content (a cell can hold several blocks and text via the Manage Cell Content dialog) and follows the cell's alignment.
tools.usage:
TINSERT
Pick a table cell: <click>
(Insert a Block in a Table Cell dialog: Name / Browse, Scale or AutoFit, Rotation angle, Overall cell alignment)

parameters.name: AutoFit
parameters.description: Scale the block so it fits the cell height/width (the default).

parameters.name: Scale / Rotation
parameters.description: Explicit values instead of AutoFit.

parameters.name: Overall cell alignment
parameters.description: Nine positions inside the cell.

tools.example:
TINSERT
(click cell A2)
(Name: VALVE_GATE, AutoFit on, Middle Center, OK)
tools.notes: Blocks with attributes show the attribute values as text in the cell and are editable through the cell's field. The same dialog is reachable from the Table Cell ribbon tab > Insert Block. A block in a cell is not a separate BlockReference for selection purposes.

tools.name: MLEADERSTYLE
tools.description: Creates and edits multileader styles, which control every visual aspect of MLEADER objects in three tabs: Leader Format (straight/spline/none, colour, linetype, lineweight, arrowhead symbol and size, break size), Leader Structure (maximum points, first/second segment angle constraints, landing and its length, annotative or scaled to layout or fixed scale) and Content (MText with style/height/colour/attachment/gap, or a Block with source block, attachment point, colour and scale - Circle, Slot, Box, Hexagon, Triangle, Detail Callout or a user block). CMLEADERSTYLE names the current style.
tools.usage:
MLEADERSTYLE
(Multileader Style Manager: styles list, Set Current, New, Modify, Delete; tabs Leader Format / Leader Structure / Content)
CMLEADERSTYLE = current style name (system variable)
MLEADERSCALE = scale factor applied to non-annotative multileaders (system variable)

parameters.name: Leader Format
parameters.description: Type Straight/Spline/None; colour, linetype, lineweight; arrowhead symbol and size; DIMBREAK gap size.

parameters.name: Leader Structure
parameters.description: Maximum leader points; first/second segment angle; automatically include landing and its length; Annotative, Scale multileaders to layout, or Specify scale.

parameters.name: Content > Multileader type
parameters.description: Mtext: default text, text style, angle, colour, height, always left justify, frame text; attachment (horizontal: Left/Right attachment options such as Top of top line, Middle of text, Underline bottom line; or vertical) and landing gap.

parameters.name: Content > Block
parameters.description: Source block (built-in bubbles or User Block with an attribute for the tag), attachment point (Center extents / Insertion point), colour, scale.

tools.example:
MLEADERSTYLE
(New: 'TAG-CIRCLE' from Standard; Content: Block > Circle, scale 1; Leader Structure: Annotative; Leader Format: arrowhead Dot small; OK, Set Current)
MLEADER (pick arrow point, pick landing, type 12 for the tag)
tools.notes: Block content with an attribute is the basis of MLEADERCOLLECT tag groups. Style overrides on individual multileaders are shown in Properties and can be removed. Import styles between drawings with DesignCenter or by inserting a template drawing.

tools.name: MLEADERALIGN
tools.description: Aligns and evenly spaces the content of several multileaders along a picked direction, relative to one chosen multileader: the text/blocks line up while the arrowheads stay put and the leader lines are re-routed. Options distribute them between two points, make the leader segments parallel, or use a fixed spacing - the standard way to tidy a column of balloon tags.
tools.usage:
MLEADERALIGN
Select multileaders: <selection> Enter
Current mode: Use current spacing
Select multileader to align to or [Options]: <pick the reference> | O
Specify direction: <drag/point>
Options: [Distribute/make leader segments Parallel/specify Spacing/Use current spacing]

parameters.name: Distribute
parameters.description: Spread the content evenly between two picked points.

parameters.name: make leader segments Parallel
parameters.description: Keep content positions but rotate the last leader segments to be parallel.

parameters.name: specify Spacing
parameters.description: Fixed distance between contents along the alignment direction.

parameters.name: Use current spacing
parameters.description: Align along the direction keeping each multileader's existing offset.

tools.example:
MLEADERALIGN
(select the six balloons) Enter
O
S
15
(pick the top balloon, drag straight down, click)
tools.notes: Works for MTEXT and block content alike. Multileaders in different styles can be aligned together. Not applicable to legacy LEADER/QLEADER objects.

tools.name: MLEADERCOLLECT
tools.description: Collects several multileaders whose content is a block (typically numbered bubbles) into a single multileader with one leader and the blocks stacked vertically, horizontally or wrapped in rows - the way part numbers pointing at the same location are combined into '3 4 7'. The original multileaders are replaced by the group.
tools.usage:
MLEADERCOLLECT
Select multileaders: <selection> Enter
Specify collected multileader location or [Vertical/Horizontal/Wrap] <Horizontal>: <point> | V | H | W
Wrap: Specify wrap width [Number] <n>:

parameters.name: Vertical / Horizontal
parameters.description: Stack the block contents in a column or a row.

parameters.name: Wrap
parameters.description: Row width or number of blocks per row before wrapping.

tools.example:
MLEADERCOLLECT
(select bubbles 3, 4 and 7) Enter
H
(click where the group should sit)
tools.notes: Only block-content multileaders in the same style can be collected; MTEXT ones are rejected. The collected object is still one MLEADER with multiple block contents and can be exploded back with EXPLODE (losing associativity).

tools.name: MLEADEREDIT
tools.description: Adds leader lines to or removes leader lines from an existing multileader, so one note can point at several features. Each added leader gets its own arrowhead and is attached to the same content; the Remove option deletes individual leaders. Also reachable from the multileader's grip menus and the Leaders panel (Add Leader / Remove Leader).
tools.usage:
MLEADEREDIT
Select a multileader: <pick>
Specify leader arrowhead location or [Remove leaders]: <point> | R
Remove: Specify leaders to remove or [Add leaders]: <pick leader line>

parameters.name: leader arrowhead location
parameters.description: Repeat to add several leaders; Enter to finish.

parameters.name: Remove leaders
parameters.description: Pick the leader lines to delete.

tools.example:
MLEADEREDIT
(pick the note)
(click the second bolt)
(click the third bolt) Enter
tools.notes: The maximum number of leader points per leader line is set in the style; the number of leader lines is unlimited. AIMLEADEREDITADD / AIMLEADEREDITREMOVE are the internal names behind the ribbon buttons.

tools.name: QLEADER
tools.description: Quick Leader: the pre-2008 leader command that draws a leader with straight or spline segments and attaches MTEXT, a tolerance frame, a block or a copy of an existing annotation, all configured in its Settings dialog. It creates a LEADER object plus a separate MTEXT (associated through the leader's annotation link), unlike MLEADER which is one object. Still widely used in scripts and older CUI macros because its prompts are simple.
tools.usage:
QLEADER  (alias LE)
Specify first leader point, or [Settings] <Settings>: <point> | Enter for settings
Specify next point: <point>
Specify next point: <point or Enter>
Specify text width <0>:
Enter first line of annotation text <Mtext>: <text> | Enter for the MTEXT editor
Settings dialog: Annotation (MText/Copy an Object/Tolerance/Block Reference/None; MText options; Annotation reuse), Leader Line & Arrow (Straight/Spline, number of points, arrowhead, angle constraints), Attachment (text position relative to leader, underline bottom line)

parameters.name: Annotation type
parameters.description: MText (default), Copy an Object, Tolerance (feature control frame), Block Reference, None (leader only).

parameters.name: Number of points
parameters.description: Limit of leader vertices (No Limit or a maximum); with 2 the command skips the extra point prompt.

parameters.name: Annotation reuse
parameters.description: Reuse Next / Reuse Current to repeat the same text on several leaders.

parameters.name: Attachment
parameters.description: Where the text attaches to the leader end (top of top line, middle, bottom...) for left and right side; Underline bottom line.

tools.example:
; Script: two-point leader with text
QLEADER
100,100
130,120

0
SEE DETAIL 5


; AutoLISP
(command "_.QLEADER" p1 p2 "" "" "NOTE" "")
tools.notes: Leader appearance follows the current DIMSTYLE (arrowhead DIMLDRBLK, size DIMASZ, text gap DIMGAP), not a multileader style. The old LEADER command is the fully manual version. Prefer MLEADER for new drawings; it is a single object, collects and aligns.

tools.name: TOLERANCE
tools.description: Creates a geometric tolerance feature control frame (GD&T) through the Geometric Tolerance dialog: a geometric characteristic symbol (position, flatness, perpendicularity...), tolerance values with diameter symbols and material condition modifiers (M, L, S), up to three datum references with modifiers, projected tolerance zone height and a datum identifier. The result is a TOLERANCE object drawn with the current dimension style's text height and gap; attach it to a leader with QLEADER (Tolerance annotation) or MLEADER.
tools.usage:
TOLERANCE  (alias TOL)
(Geometric Tolerance dialog: Sym, Tolerance 1 / Tolerance 2 [dia, value, MC], Datum 1 / 2 / 3 [letter, MC], Height, Projected Tolerance Zone, Datum Identifier)
Specify tolerance location: <point>

parameters.name: Sym
parameters.description: Click to pick the characteristic symbol from the Symbol palette (position, concentricity, symmetry, parallelism, perpendicularity, angularity, cylindricity, flatness, circularity, straightness, profile of surface/line, circular/total runout).

parameters.name: Tolerance 1/2
parameters.description: Optional diameter symbol, the value, and material condition (Maximum, Least, Regardless of feature size).

parameters.name: Datum 1/2/3
parameters.description: Datum letters with optional material condition; composite frames use the second row.

parameters.name: Height / Projected Tolerance Zone
parameters.description: Projected zone height and the P symbol.

parameters.name: Datum Identifier
parameters.description: Creates a datum feature symbol (e.g. -A-) instead of a tolerance.

tools.example:
TOLERANCE
(Sym: position; Tolerance 1: dia, 0.25, M; Datum 1: A; Datum 2: B; Datum 3: C; OK)
(click below the hole dimension)
tools.notes: The frame's text height and gap come from DIMTXT/DIMGAP of the current style, so set the style before creating frames. The DXF entity is TOLERANCE with the content encoded in group 1 using control codes ({\Fgdt;j} etc.). Not associative to geometry.

tools.name: CENTERMARK
tools.description: Creates an associative centre mark on a circle, arc or polyline arc (2017+): a cross whose size, gap, extension lines, linetype and layer come from the CENTER* system variables, and which follows the circle when it is moved or resized. Grips lengthen the extension lines; the Properties palette exposes cross size, gap, extensions and rotation. CENTERLINE is the companion for two lines; both replace the legacy DIMCENTER-style marks made of plain lines.
tools.usage:
CENTERMARK
Select circle or arc to add center mark: <pick> (repeat, Enter to finish)
System variables: CENTERMARKEXE (1 draw extension lines), CENTEREXE (extension beyond the object), CENTERCROSSSIZE (cross length, e.g. 0.1x = 10% of radius), CENTERCROSSGAP (gap between cross and extensions), CENTERLTYPE, CENTERLTSCALE, CENTERLAYER

parameters.name: CENTERCROSSSIZE / CENTERCROSSGAP
parameters.description: Absolute values or, with an x suffix, multiples of the circle radius (default 0.1x and 0.05x).

parameters.name: CENTERMARKEXE
parameters.description: 1 extension lines drawn to CENTEREXE beyond the circle, 0 cross only.

parameters.name: CENTERLTYPE / CENTERLTYPEFILE
parameters.description: Linetype (default CENTER2) loaded from the named .lin file if missing.

parameters.name: CENTERLAYER
parameters.description: Layer for new centre marks and centrelines; '.' means current layer.

tools.example:
CENTERLAYER CENTER
CENTERCROSSSIZE 0.1x
CENTERMARK
(click each bolt hole) Enter
tools.notes: Centre marks are their own object type (CENTERMARK / CENTERLINE), not lines - they can be exploded to lines when sending to systems that cannot read them. CENTERRESET reapplies CENTEREXE after grip edits; CENTERDISASSOCIATE / CENTERREASSOCIATE manage the link to the geometry.

tools.name: CENTERLINE
tools.description: Creates an associative centreline between two selected lines or polyline segments (2017+), bisecting the angle between them (parallel lines get a midline) and extending past their ends by CENTEREXE. The centreline follows the lines when they move, uses CENTERLTYPE on CENTERLAYER and has grips to lengthen its ends. Typical for shafts, slots and symmetric parts in mechanical drawings.
tools.usage:
CENTERLINE
Select first line: <pick>
Select second line: <pick>

parameters.name: CENTEREXE
parameters.description: How far the centreline extends past the ends of the selected lines (drawing units).

parameters.name: CENTERLTSCALE
parameters.description: Linetype scale applied to centre marks and centrelines (default 1).

tools.example:
CENTERLINE
(pick the top edge of the shaft)
(pick the bottom edge)
tools.notes: Both objects must be lines or linear polyline segments; arcs use CENTERMARK. Crossing lines give a bisector centreline. Available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: CENTERRESET
tools.description: Resets the extension lines of selected centre marks and centrelines to the current CENTEREXE value after they have been grip-stretched, and re-centres a mark whose circle has changed. CENTERDISASSOCIATE breaks the link between a centre mark/centreline and its geometry (leaving a static object) and CENTERREASSOCIATE re-links a disassociated one to a circle/arc or pair of lines.
tools.usage:
CENTERRESET
Select center marks or centerlines to reset: <selection> Enter
CENTERDISASSOCIATE
Select center marks or centerlines to disassociate: <selection> Enter
CENTERREASSOCIATE
Select center mark or centerline to associate: <pick>  then Select circle or arc / Select first line, second line
tools.example:
CENTEREXE 5
CENTERRESET
(select all centre marks) Enter
tools.notes: Disassociated centre marks show an exclamation badge when the annotation monitor is on. After a circle is erased its centre mark remains, disassociated.

tools.name: DIMTEDIT
tools.description: Moves or rotates the text of one dimension: drag it to a new position along or off the dimension line, force it Left, Right or Center on the line, return it Home (the style's default position) or set a text Angle. It changes the dimension's text-position overrides without touching the style and is what the ribbon's text position buttons run. DIMEDIT handles the text content and extension lines instead.
tools.usage:
DIMTEDIT
Select dimension: <pick>
Specify new location for dimension text or [Left/Right/Center/Home/Angle]: <point> | L | R | C | H | A

parameters.name: Left / Right / Center
parameters.description: Justify the text along the dimension line (linear, radial and diameter only).

parameters.name: Home
parameters.description: Restore the default position defined by DIMJUST/DIMTAD/DIMTMOVE; also clears rotation.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Rotate the text; 0 returns it to the style's orientation.

parameters.name: DIMTMOVE
parameters.description: System variable deciding what moving text does: 0 dimension line moves with it, 1 adds a leader, 2 text moves freely.

tools.example:
DIMTEDIT
(pick the crowded dimension)
R

; put text back where the style wants it on a whole selection
DIMEDIT H (select dimensions)
tools.notes: Grip-editing the text grip does the same interactively. Moving text with DIMTMOVE 0 shifts the dimension line, which surprises people expecting only the text to move.

tools.name: DIMINSPECT
tools.description: Adds or removes an inspection frame on existing dimensions: a round, angular or plain frame that divides the dimension into the inspection label, the dimension value and the inspection rate (e.g. 100%), as used to flag dimensions that must be checked in production. The frame is part of the dimension object and follows its text.
tools.usage:
DIMINSPECT
(Inspection Dimension dialog: Select dimensions button, Shape [Round/Angular/None], Label field, Inspection rate field, Remove Inspection button)

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.description: Round (capsule), Angular (hexagonal ends) or None (vertical bars only).

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: Text in the left cell, e.g. an inspection reference.

parameters.name: Inspection rate
parameters.description: Text in the right cell; the default 100% means every part is inspected.

tools.example:
DIMINSPECT
(Select dimensions: pick the bore diameter; Shape Round; Label A; Rate 100%; OK)
tools.notes: Command-line equivalent: -DIMINSPECT with Add/Remove options. Inspection frames are supported in the ActiveX AcadDimension Inspection properties (InspectionLabel, InspectionRate, InspectionFrame).

tools.name: DIMREASSOCIATE
tools.description: Re-links dimensions that lost their associativity (after STRETCH with osnaps off, EXPLODE/recreate, or copying from another drawing) to points on geometry, one extension-line origin at a time, marking each point with an X so you know which one is being re-associated; a boxed X means it is already associative. The Disassociated option selects all non-associative dimensions in one go. DIMDISASSOCIATE does the opposite, and DIMASSOC decides whether new dimensions are associative at all.
tools.usage:
DIMREASSOCIATE
Select objects or [Disassociated]: <dimensions> | D
(for each dimension) Specify first extension line origin or [Select object] <next>: <osnap point on geometry> | S | Enter to skip
Specify second extension line origin <next>: ...
DIMDISASSOCIATE
Select dimensions to disassociate: <selection> Enter

parameters.name: Disassociated
parameters.description: Automatically select every dimension in the drawing that is not fully associative.

parameters.name: Select object
parameters.description: Associate to a whole object (line, arc, circle) instead of a point.

parameters.name: DIMASSOC
parameters.description: 2 associative (default), 1 non-associative but one object, 0 exploded into lines and text.

tools.example:
DIMREASSOCIATE
D
(pick END of the plate corner)
(pick END of the other corner)
Enter (skip the next dimension)
tools.notes: Only osnapped points (or Select object) create associations; a freehand point is refused. Associativity to xref geometry is supported; to blocks it is to the reference's geometry. The annotation monitor (ANNOMONITOR 1) flags disassociated dimensions with a badge.

tools.name: DIMREGEN
tools.description: Updates the location of all associative dimensions so they match the geometry after events that do not trigger an automatic update: geometry moved in an xref that was reloaded, dimensions in paper space measuring model-space objects after the viewport was panned or zoomed, or objects edited through a program that skipped the reactor. It is cheap and safe to run in any script after such edits.
tools.usage: DIMREGEN  (no prompts)
tools.example:
-XREF R *
DIMREGEN
QSAVE
tools.notes: Only associative dimensions (DIMASSOC 2) are affected. Trans-spatial dimensions (paper-space dimensions of model-space objects) are the main case; they otherwise stay put when the viewport view changes until DIMREGEN or a plot.

tools.name: DIMJOGLINE
tools.description: Adds a jog (zigzag) symbol to a linear or aligned dimension to indicate that the drawn length is foreshortened - the feature is longer than shown - or removes one. The jog is placed at a picked point or at the midpoint by default; its height is controlled by the style's DIMJOGANG-independent linear jog factor (Linear Jog Size in DIMSTYLE). DIMJOGGED is different: it creates a jogged radius dimension for large arcs.
tools.usage:
DIMJOGLINE
Select dimension to add jog or [Remove]: <pick> | R
Specify jog location (or press Enter): <point> | Enter for the midpoint

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.description: Delete the jog from a selected dimension.

parameters.name: Jog height factor
parameters.description: DIMSTYLE > Symbols and Arrows > Linear Jog Dimension: jog height as a multiple of text height.

tools.example:
DIMLINEAR 0,0 500,0 0,-20
DIMJOGLINE
(pick it)

(jog placed at the middle)
tools.notes: The measured value is unchanged; override the text with DIMEDIT N or the Text property if a longer true length must be shown. Works on DIMLINEAR/DIMALIGNED dimensions only.

tools.name: DIMOVERRIDE
tools.description: Applies dimension-variable overrides to selected dimensions without changing their style - e.g. set DIMTAD (text above line) or DIMSE1 (suppress first extension line) on a few dimensions - or clears every override so the dimensions return to their style. Overrides are stored on the dimension as xdata and show in Properties; -DIMSTYLE Apply can push a style back onto dimensions in the same way.
tools.usage:
DIMOVERRIDE  (alias DOV)
Enter dimension variable name to override or [Clear]: <DIMxxx> | C
Enter new value for dimension variable <current>: <value>
Enter dimension variable name to override: (more, or Enter)
Select objects: <dimensions> Enter
Clear: Select objects: (removes all overrides)

parameters.name: dimension variable
parameters.description: Any DIM* system variable: DIMTAD, DIMTIX, DIMSE1/DIMSE2, DIMDEC, DIMLFAC, DIMTOFL, DIMSCALE, DIMCLRD...

parameters.name: Clear
parameters.description: Remove every override from the selected dimensions.

tools.example:
DIMOVERRIDE
DIMSE1
1
DIMSE2
1

(select the two dimensions whose extension lines clash with the wall) Enter
tools.notes: Setting a DIM* variable at the command line while no command is active creates a style override on the current style (shown in DIMSTYLE as <style overrides>) affecting new dimensions - a different thing. To find dimensions with overrides use QSELECT or the annotation monitor.

tools.name: DIMEX
tools.description: Express Tools pair for moving dimension styles between drawings without templates or DesignCenter: DIMEX writes selected dimension styles (all DIM* values, plus optionally text styles) to a .dim text file and DIMIM reads such a file, creating or overwriting the styles in the current drawing. Because the .dim file is plain text it can be version-controlled and diffed.
tools.usage:
DIMEX
(Dimension Style Export dialog: Export filename .dim, Available dimension styles list, Text style options [Full text style information / Text style name only])
DIMIM
(Dimension Style Import dialog: Import filename .dim, Import options [Keep the existing style / Overwrite existing style])

parameters.name: Full text style information
parameters.description: Also export the text styles used by the dimension styles so DIMIM recreates them.

parameters.name: Overwrite existing style
parameters.description: Replace styles of the same name in the target drawing.

tools.example:
DIMEX -> C:\std\ISO-25.dim (select ISO-25 and ISO-25-MECH, Full text style information)
(in another drawing) DIMIM -> C:\std\ISO-25.dim, Overwrite
tools.notes: Child sub-styles (ISO-25$0 for linear etc.) are exported with the parent. The core alternative is the DIMSTYLE dialog's Import through DesignCenter, or CHECKSTANDARDS with a .dws file. Not in LT.

tools.name: MLEDIT
tools.description: Edits the intersections and vertices of multilines (MLINE objects) through the Multilines Edit Tools dialog: closed/open/merged crosses and tees for two crossing multilines, corner joints, add or delete vertex, cut single/cut all elements between two points, and weld all to close cuts. -MLEDIT offers the same operations as keywords for scripts. It is the only way to clean up wall intersections drawn with MLINE, because TRIM and FILLET do not operate on multilines.
tools.usage:
MLEDIT
(Multilines Edit Tools dialog: Closed Cross, Open Cross, Merged Cross, Closed Tee, Open Tee, Merged Tee, Corner Joint, Add Vertex, Delete Vertex, Cut Single, Cut All, Weld All)
Select first mline: / Select second mline:
-MLEDIT
Enter mline editing option [CC/OC/MC/CT/OT/MT/CJ/AV/DV/CS/CA/WA]:

parameters.name: Crosses (CC/OC/MC)
parameters.description: Closed: first mline is cut by the second; Open: outer elements of both are cut; Merged: outer elements cut, inner elements joined.

parameters.name: Tees (CT/OT/MT)
parameters.description: Same three variants where the first mline ends at the second.

parameters.name: Corner Joint (CJ)
parameters.description: Trim or extend two multilines to form a clean corner.

parameters.name: Add / Delete Vertex (AV/DV)
parameters.description: Insert or remove a vertex at a picked point.

parameters.name: Cut Single / Cut All / Weld All (CS/CA/WA)
parameters.description: Open a gap in one element or all elements between two points, or close such gaps.

tools.example:
-MLEDIT
OT
(pick the partition wall near the junction)
(pick the external wall)
tools.notes: Element properties (offsets, colours, linetypes) come from the MLSTYLE and cannot be changed on an existing mline unless the style is redefined while no mlines use it. Multilines explode into plain lines.

tools.name: ANNORESET
tools.description: Resets the position of every scale representation of selected annotative objects to match the position of the current-scale representation. Annotative text, blocks and dimensions store a separate location per scale (so labels can be nudged apart at 1:100 but not at 1:50); after moving one representation the others may drift, and ANNORESET aligns them all again.
tools.usage:
ANNORESET
Select annotative objects: <selection> Enter
tools.example:
ANNORESET
(select all room tags) Enter
tools.notes: Only affects objects that have more than one scale representation. The ribbon equivalent is Annotate > Annotation Scaling > Sync Scale Positions. SELECTIONANNODISPLAY shows the alternate representations faded when an object is selected.

tools.name: ANNOUPDATE
tools.description: Updates selected annotative objects to the current properties of their style: when a text style or dimension style is changed to or from annotative, or its paper height is edited, existing objects keep their old settings until ANNOUPDATE (or the drawing is regenerated in some cases). It also converts non-annotative text to annotative when its style became annotative, giving the object the current scale.
tools.usage:
ANNOUPDATE
Select objects: <selection or ALL> Enter
tools.example:
STYLE (make 'NOTES' annotative, paper height 2.5)
ANNOUPDATE
ALL
tools.notes: Objects updated this way get the current annotation scale (CANNOSCALE) only; add further scales with OBJECTSCALE or by changing the scale with ANNOAUTOSCALE on.

tools.name: SCALELISTEDIT
tools.description: Edits the drawing's list of annotation and viewport scales (the list shown in the status-bar scale menu, VPORTS scale, PLOT and OBJECTSCALE): add named scales such as 1:75 or 1"=20', edit, reorder, delete, or reset to the default list defined in Options > User Preferences > Default Scale List. Trimming the list to the project's scales removes clutter and the Reset also purges the xref-imported scales that bloat drawings. -SCALELISTEDIT is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
SCALELISTEDIT
(Edit Drawing Scales dialog: Scale List, Add, Edit, Move Up, Move Down, Delete, Reset)
-SCALELISTEDIT
Enter option [?/Add/Delete/Reset/Exit] <Add>:
Add: Enter name for new scale: 1:75   Enter scale ratio (paper:drawing) <1:1>: 1:75

parameters.name: Add
parameters.description: Name displayed in lists and the paper:drawing ratio.

parameters.name: Delete
parameters.description: Only scales not used by any annotative object or viewport can be deleted.

parameters.name: Reset
parameters.description: Replace the list with the default metric or imperial list (MEASUREMENT decides) and remove unused custom scales - the cure for hundreds of XREF-imported scales.

parameters.name: HIDEXREFSCALES
parameters.description: 1 (default) hides scales that came in with xrefs from the lists.

tools.example:
-SCALELISTEDIT
R
Y
-SCALELISTEDIT
A
1:75
1:75
E
tools.notes: The list is stored in the drawing; put the project list in the template. The default list itself is edited in OPTIONS (User Preferences tab > Default Scale List), not here.

tools.name: ANNOALLVISIBLE
tools.description: Controls whether annotative objects that do not support the current annotation scale are still displayed: 1 shows every annotative object regardless of scale (and shows the current-scale representation); 0 hides objects lacking the current scale - the intended production setting, so a 1:50 viewport only shows 1:50 annotations. Saved per drawing and separately for model space and each layout; the status-bar Annotation Visibility button toggles it.
tools.usage:
ANNOALLVISIBLE = 0 | 1
0 = only annotative objects that have the current annotation scale are shown
1 = all annotative objects shown (default in new drawings)

parameters.description: Scale-filtered display; objects without the current scale vanish (they are not deleted).
Everything visible; objects lacking the current scale are shown using their nearest representation.

tools.example:
; make a viewport show only its own scale's annotations
MSPACE
CANNOSCALE 1:50
ANNOALLVISIBLE 0
tools.notes: Objects that seem to disappear after a scale change are the classic symptom of ANNOALLVISIBLE 0 plus missing object scales - add the scale with OBJECTSCALE rather than switching to 1. In the Core Console leave it at 1 when plotting sets with mixed scales unless every object has been assigned its scales.

tools.name: ANNOAUTOSCALE
tools.description: When the annotation scale is changed (status bar, CANNOSCALE, viewport scale), decides whether the new scale is added automatically to existing annotative objects so they get a representation at that scale: 0 off; 1-4 on, differing in which layer states are excluded; negative values remember the mode while switched off (the status-bar Add Scales button toggles the sign). Leaving it on while browsing scales adds many unwanted scales to every object, which bloats drawings.
tools.usage:
ANNOAUTOSCALE = -4 .. 4
 1 / -1: add to annotative objects that support it, except those on layers turned off, frozen, locked or viewport-frozen
 2 / -2: except objects on layers off, frozen or viewport-frozen
 3 / -3: except objects on locked layers
 4 / -4: add to all annotative objects
 0: off (no scales added)
negative = off but the positive mode is remembered

parameters.name: positive
parameters.description: Automatic scale addition is active.

parameters.name: negative
parameters.description: Inactive; toggled back on by the status-bar button.
Disabled entirely.

tools.example:
; project standard: never add scales automatically
ANNOAUTOSCALE -4
; add scales explicitly instead
OBJECTSCALE (select) A 1:20
tools.notes: Registry setting, so it applies to all drawings. Removing stray scales afterwards is done with OBJECTSCALE Delete or the Annotative Object Scale dialog; SCALELISTEDIT Reset removes unused scales from the list, not from objects.

tools.name: TEXTLAYER
tools.description: One of the family of 'default layer' system variables that put new annotation on a fixed layer regardless of the current layer: TEXTLAYER (text and MTEXT, 2020.1), DIMLAYER (dimensions, 2016), MLEADERLAYER (multileaders, 2025.1), TABLELAYER (tables, 2026.1), REVCLOUDLAYER (revision clouds, 2026.1), VIEWPORTLAYER (layout viewports, 2026.1), CENTERLAYER (centre marks/lines, 2017), HPLAYER (hatches, 2015) and XREFLAYER (new xrefs, 2018.1). A value of '.' (a period) means use the current layer; a non-existent layer is created on first use.
tools.usage:
TEXTLAYER = "<layer name>" | "."
DIMLAYER / MLEADERLAYER / TABLELAYER / REVCLOUDLAYER / VIEWPORTLAYER / CENTERLAYER / HPLAYER / XREFLAYER = "<layer name>" | "."

parameters.name: layer name
parameters.description: Objects of that type are created on this layer; it is created if missing (with default properties).
Use the current layer (CLAYER) - the default behaviour.

tools.example:
; template setup script
TEXTLAYER A-ANNO-TEXT
DIMLAYER A-ANNO-DIMS
MLEADERLAYER A-ANNO-NOTE
HPLAYER A-PATT
XREFLAYER X-REF
VIEWPORTLAYER DEFPOINTS
tools.notes: All are saved in the drawing, so set them in the template. Scripts that rely on CLAYER for placing text must reset TEXTLAYER to '.' first. DIMLAYER is also an option inside the DIM command.

tools.name: MTEXT formatting codes
tools.description: The inline control codes stored in MTEXT, multileader and attribute strings (visible in entget group 1/3 and in the ActiveX TextString): they set fonts, height, colour, width, oblique, stacking, paragraphs and underline within one object. Programs that write MTEXT must emit these codes; programs that read text must strip them (or use vla-get-TextString on a temporary copy after explode). Special symbol codes (%%c, %%d, %%p) work in both TEXT and MTEXT, and Unicode escapes \U+xxxx insert any character.
tools.usage:
\P            new paragraph (line break)
\~            non-breaking space
\\  \{  \}    literal backslash and braces
{ ... }       group whose formatting ends at the closing brace
\fArial|b1|i0|c0|p34;   font (b bold, i italic, c charset, p pitch)   \Fromans.shx;   SHX font
\Hn;  \Hnx;   height (absolute, or relative x factor)      \Wn;  width factor
\Cn;          colour index (\C1;) or \c<truecolor>;         \Tn;  tracking     \Qn;  oblique angle
\L ... \l     underline    \O ... \o overline    \K ... \k strikethrough
\S1/2;  \S1^2;  \S+0.1^-0.2;   stacked fraction (/ diagonal, ^ vertical, # slash)  ; \A0; \A1; \A2; vertical alignment bottom/center/top of stacked text

parameters.name: Column codes
parameters.description: Static and dynamic MTEXT columns are stored as \pxsm..; and \N (column break) in the string, plus column settings on the object.

parameters.name: Background mask
parameters.description: Not a code - a property (BackgroundFill, group 90/63/45 in DXF).

parameters.name: Stripping codes
parameters.description: Common LISP approach: regular-expression replace via vlax-create-object VBScript.RegExp, or the undocumented but stable pattern of removing \\[^;]*; sequences and braces.

tools.notes: Fonts named in \f must exist or FONTALT is substituted. Width factor and height codes inside groups are the reason FIND sometimes fails to match text that looks contiguous. The MTEXT editor shows none of this; view the raw string with LIST or (entget).
